name: go5_saturate
hypothesis: 9x9 model still 0/20 vs GnuGo L1 even at loss 0.55. Switching to 5x5 to validate the algorithm can beat GnuGo at ALL before scaling up. Two configs: 20b×256f (33M params, absurdly large) and 10b×128f (3M params). If the big model beats GnuGo on 5x5, we know the algorithm works and capacity is the key. If it doesn't, the problem is fundamental.
estimated_time: 4-8h total (5x5 is very fast: ~25 actions, short games). Two configs × 500 iters.
success_criteria: Beat GnuGo Level 1 on 5x5 (>50% in 20 games). Stretch: beat Level 5.

infra_requirements.gpu: A100 80GB or any fast GPU — 5x5 is small, even A4000 would be fast
infra_requirements.gnugo: apt-get install -y gnugo (CRITICAL — script runs GnuGo eval automatically)
infra_requirements.git_pull: MUST git pull to get go5 game registration and eval --use-ownership-head flag

notes: This is a validation experiment. 5x5 Go is simple enough that a 33M param model should dominate. If it can't beat GnuGo L1 on 5x5, our training pipeline has a fundamental issue beyond model capacity. REQUIRES: git pull for go5 registration + eval_vs_gnugo.py ownership flag.
